pattern: does not conform to the 'Sendable' protocol
scope: a completion's request keeps its sending convention where the generated method passes it on, and an observing owner, which keeps the request, has it declare Sendable, which the compiler checks from its stored fields

pattern: PreparationRejection
scope: router candidates share a failure only when their spellings name one type by a compiler-checked equivalence: an alias, a qualified name, sugar, any, a composition's or attributes' order, a nested composition flattened and a repeated member, parentheses, a throw of Never or any Error, Swift's metatype rule, and the concrete metatype of a sugared standard type; any other difference keeps two failures

pattern: _TriggerPayloadMatchesDeclaration
scope: the witness that an edge takes its Input case's payload infers the payload from the case's constructor alone and compares it with the parameter in a statement of its own, so no optional promotion, erasure, or function conversion adapts one to the other

pattern: succeeds without output, as its onSuccess: edges and routers take none
scope: where the macro cannot confirm an operation's Output, the success edges and routers decide whether a success carries a value, and the expansion checks the type

pattern: has no onFailure: edge or router, so the macro reads its Failure as Never
scope: where the macro cannot confirm an operation's Failure or Output, its onFailure: and onSuccess: edges and routers decide whether that outcome happens, and the expansion checks the type

pattern: may allow it to escape
scope: a request that carries an input and a work that can succeed store their input and output through a generic parameter, so a closure the macro cannot see is stored without @escaping and a non-escaping one is rejected

pattern: reads this type as the standard library's Never, but it resolves to a different type
scope: a router with no edge to choose shows that the spelling it throws names a type with values, every function that throws the same spelling is revised with it, and each check belongs to its own declaration

pattern: Sendable
scope: a request an observing owner keeps and passes to a sending parameter declares Sendable, which the compiler checks from its stored fields, public or not

pattern: Sendable
scope: an Owned router's sending request is transferred once unless an edge it selects also takes it, which needs the request to be Sendable

pattern: reads this value with its source phase
scope: an Owned router reads its payload or request with its source phase, so an edge it selects takes the value as sending only when the value or the phase is Sendable, which a generated check reports

pattern: names another type inside the schema
scope: every expansion checks the schema's name in type position, where a value of that name is no candidate, and names the schema through its alias where an expression needs it

pattern: nests too deeply, or reaches its type through too many aliases
scope: a chain of aliases that each name the next reads without nesting at any length, and a reading that passes a step or nesting budget is diagnosed at its declaration, never guessed

pattern: PreparationRejection
scope: two failures are one only when the macro proves it, so a qualified custom attribute names the type its own scope finds and two such spellings in different scopes stay distinct

pattern: succeeds with output, so its success edge takes the output, unlabeled, after the source
scope: a success edge of an operation that succeeds with output takes the output unlabeled before its request:, so one that takes only the request is diagnosed at the request

pattern: Take the request last, labeled request:, after the source and the operation.s failure
scope: a completion takes its request last, after the source and the outcome, which the declaration diagnoses otherwise

pattern: Only a completion edge or router takes its operation.s request, labeled request:
scope: a function an input triggers takes no request, so a request: label there is diagnosed

pattern: _stateMachineTakesOutput' is unavailable: .*take the request with the argument label request:
scope: an unlabeled parameter after the source is the output, the request's own type included, and the witness that compares it with the Output names the label a request takes

pattern: _stateMachineTakesOutput' is unavailable
scope: the review's spellings: a schema alias named like the request, an Output that is the request's backing type, and an alias of the generated request whose Output an extension makes Void, each taking the role its label says

pattern: has no Key and takes no input, so its completion carries no request
scope: an operation without a key or an input has no request, so a request: parameter is diagnosed whatever it spells

pattern: does not conform to (the )?.Hashable.|requires that .* conform to .Hashable.
scope: a request that carries only a key is Hashable and Sendable, and one that carries an input is Hashable exactly when its input is

pattern: takes Never as its input
scope: an unkeyed operation whose completion takes its request carries its input, so carriage is decided first and a carried input the macro reads as Void through a name it cannot confirm is checked not to be Never

pattern: Input is noncopyable, which only Owned supports
scope: an Owned verb repeats the ownership its transition declares for a payload, so a noncopyable input moves through Owned, and an owner that keeps inputs rejects a noncopyable Input where it is declared

pattern: cannot be both given away and passed on
scope: an Owned router's method lends a noncopyable payload to the router and passes it on, so a router that consumes it, leaving nothing for the edge it selects, is rejected by a check that names the cause

pattern: borrowed and cannot be consumed
scope: an Owned routed method borrows its payload when the router and every edge it may select borrow it, so a borrowing caller can call it, and consumes it when an edge consumes it

pattern: 'consuming' cannot be applied to nonescaping closure
scope: an Owned routed method and its direct verbs take a nonescaping closure payload the ways the router and its edges may, plain, sending, borrowing, __owned, and __shared sending, so the expansion compiles whenever the authored functions do, and a consuming nonescaping closure is Swift's own rejection at the authored function

pattern: passing non-escaping parameter 'work' to function expecting an '@escaping' closure
scope: a router and its edges that differ in taking a closure payload @escaping, borrowing or __shared, with or without sending, give an Owned routed method that takes the payload escaping and compiles, so a caller passes an escaping closure, which may be one it only borrows

pattern: borrowed and cannot be consumed
scope: an Owned router that consumes a payload its edges then borrow gets an implicit copy from a plain method parameter, so a borrowing caller can route it, while an edge that consumes it, every function declaring an ownership, makes the method consume it

pattern: succeeds with output, so its success edge takes the output, unlabeled, after the source
scope: the argument label decides a completion parameter's role: an unlabeled parameter after the source is the output, whatever it spells, the request's own type included, and the parameter labeled request: is the request, through any alias

pattern: cannot be converted to error type
scope: a tuple element's wildcard label is no label, as Swift reads it, so (_: A, B) and (A, B) are one failure and (_: ()) is Void, while a backticked label is its own

pattern: Put this construction in a static function that returns Idle
scope: an initial case that qualifies its payload, as Form.Idle or Self.Idle, names the one phase payload, whose default construction every fresh entry point spells once through the schema's alias

pattern: reads this value with the other value it passes on
scope: an Owned router joins every value it reads without sending, so an edge it selects that sends one while another stays in use needs one of the two Sendable, which a generated check reports however Sendable the source phase is

pattern: reads this value with its source phase
scope: a request is Sendable exactly when its input is, through the runtime's conditional conformance, so a public request that carries an Int passes through a router to edges that send it beside a phase that is not Sendable

pattern: takes this value as sending and another takes it without
scope: a value one edge an Owned router may select sends while another reads it must be Sendable, even when the router never takes it, because the router's method keeps a value it may give away

pattern: has no onSuccess: edge or router
scope: a standard-library name confirms its kind only from the macro's table: UnboundedRange is the function type it aliases, so a driver keeps it, and another standard name such as the caseless Unicode is checked wherever the shape rests on it

pattern: Destination 'Swift\.Int' is not a phase payload type declared in this schema
scope: parentheses around a phase payload, source, destination, router choice, effect type, or the base of a member type change no shape the macro reads; a parenthesized destination that is no phase is diagnosed by its plain spelling

pattern: Use a plain or borrowing phase payload as the source parameter
scope: a __shared source lends it as borrowing does and an .ownedOnly __owned source takes it as consuming does; an __owned source outside .ownedOnly is diagnosed as consuming is

pattern: Remove '@available' and give the schema this availability instead
scope: generated members have only the schema's availability, so an authored function cannot carry @available, which the macro cannot compare with the deployment target; a schema whose availability is above the client's deployment target, with its payload types annotated, compiles

pattern: Remove '@uiActor': generated code calls this function from nonisolated code
scope: an authored function takes only the macro's markers and Swift's @discardableResult, @inlinable, @inline, and @usableFromInline, so a custom attribute is refused whatever its capitalization

pattern: Declare 'Notes' public: the public schema 'Approval' generates public members that name it
scope: a public schema requires its access of the declarations its generated signatures name, each resolved where its spelling is written, so a private helper sharing a basename with a public payload compiles and a type named through a path needs the access at every step

pattern: Use .parallel\(limit: N\) with a positive integer literal representable as Int
scope: an admission limit is read as Swift reads an integer literal, with separators or in another base, and a limit of zero in any spelling is refused

pattern: The name .* is not in Unicode Normalization Form C; spell it
scope: the Normalization Form C rule covers the names the macro interprets, so a function body, an accessor, and a closure may call a declaration whose name is not composed, while a signature that names it is refused

pattern: 'start' is deprecated: renamed to 'begin'
scope: a deprecated edge, router, completion edge, or restoration function deprecates only the generated public members named for it, with the authored message or rename; generated code calls the functions through a witnessed requirement, so the schema compiles with warnings as errors, and a caller that is not deprecated gets Swift's deprecation

pattern: Remove '@available' and give the schema this availability instead
scope: a deprecation on every platform is accepted on an authored function, and a deprecation from a platform version, which is availability the macro cannot compare with the deployment target, is refused

pattern: Remove 'renamed:': the restoring initializers and resets this deprecation marks keep their names
scope: a deprecated restoration function deprecates the restoring initializers and resets with its message, and its deprecation cannot rename them

pattern: 'post\(\)' is deprecated: Use submit\.
scope: a deprecation's options after * are read by kind in any order, as Swift reads them, and the generated methods repeat the attribute as written

pattern: Write the bare name of the replacement edge in 'renamed:'
scope: a rename is accepted only as the bare name of another edge with a generated method wherever the deprecated one has, so the fix-it's call compiles. A qualified or labeled target is refused at its string

pattern: The schema name is reserved or shadowed by a direct member; choose a distinct domain name
scope: a value or method named like the schema hides nothing generated code looks up as a type, and a type of that name directly inside the schema is refused

pattern: Declare 'Hidden' public: the public schema 'Flow' generates public members that name it
scope: a member named through a namespace alias needs the public schema's access, as it does through the type's own name

pattern: Declare 'Hidden' public: the public schema 'Flow' generates public members that name it
scope: a member of a generic type named through a specialized alias or a specialization written in place needs the public schema's access, since the arguments do not change which declaration it is

pattern: Declare 'Sendable' public: the public schema 'Flow' generates public members that name it
scope: a built-in attribute's name names no declaration, so a helper named Sendable needs no access, while a type reference to it does

pattern: Take this payload without '@autoclosure'
scope: a built-in attribute's name and a member read in an attribute's arguments mean the same with redundant backticks, so an escaped attribute is accepted or refused as its bare spelling is
